title: Why Krishna keeps working
hook: who is the service for? the Gita draws the circle wider than anyone asked
carry: lokasangraha: act so the world holds together
tomorrow: a plan so big it's dead by spring. what does the Gita say?

segments.voice: Yesterday, karma: Arjuna dropped his bow, and Krishna said no one can stop acting, so a year of service starts with the work already in your hands. Today the week comes back, with one more ring.

Every plan has a line near the top: who is this for? A food drive is for the hungry. A tutoring hour is for one kid. Krishna answers that line for the path of action, and his answer is wider than anyone asked. Act, he tells Arjuna, with your eye on holding the world together.
screen: `WHO IS THIS FOR?` → `ONE KID, ONE FOOD DRIVE.` → `HOLD THE WORLD TOGETHER.`

segments.voice: The Sanskrit is lokasangraha: loka, the world and the people in it; sangraha, a holding together. In chapter three of the Gita, Krishna gives the reason, and then he points at himself. Whatever a great person does, others do too; the world follows the standard that person sets. And, Krishna says, there's nothing in all the worlds I need to do, nothing I lack, and still I keep working. If I stopped, people everywhere would follow my path, and the worlds would fall apart. God himself keeps working, for the sake of everyone watching. That's the teaching: in karma yoga, service reaches the one person helped, and also everyone who sees how it's done. Now the week, one more pass. Kundalini climbs, lotus by lotus, to the crown, where Shakti and Shiva are one. Seed sounds on the petals: in a mantra, the sound itself is sacred. A moon, a sun, and Ekalavya before his clay teacher: some practices are handed on, guru to student. A rain cloud at the navel: in dhyana, you hold the form as it's given. The way home, down the same road, because the everyday world is Shakti too. And Arjuna's dropped bow: no one can stop acting, so do your work and let go of the fruits.
screen: `LOKASANGRAHA: HOLDING THE WORLD.` · `OTHERS FOLLOW THE STANDARD SET.` · `KRISHNA KEEPS WORKING.` · `THE WEEK, ONE MORE PASS.` · then, large: `A WIDER CIRCLE.`

segments.voice: On a scrap of paper, draw three rings, one inside the next. In the center write one person you serve, in the middle ring the people who see you do it, and leave the outer ring open for the world. Rest your eyes on all three together for the rest of the sit.
Karma: action, and in the Gita, action done with an eye on lokasangraha, the holding together of the world.
Last line of the week: lokasangraha, act so the world holds together. Even Krishna keeps working. Seven days, and a wider circle.

howItsDone: Some Hindus think of service as including the example it sets for children, students and coworkers, reading the Gita's lokasangraha as care for the world that watches and follows.
